The Terms of a Derivative of the Expectation of a Product of Two Scores

Source: R/d34e_truncated.R
d34e_plan.Rd

Expands \(\partial_S E[\ell_a \ell_b]\) as the expectation of a polynomial in the derivatives of the log-density \(\ell\).

Usage

d34e_plan(P, a, b, S)

Arguments

P

The parameter names.

a, b

The indices of the pair.

S

The integer indices of the derivative, with repetition.

Value

A list with coef, the coefficient of each term, factors, a list of the keys of each term's factors, and blocks, a named list giving the parameter names of each key.

Details

With \(f = e^{\ell}\) the derivative of the density in the parameters of a multiset \(R\) is \(f\) times the complete Bell polynomial \(Y_R\) of the derivatives of \(\ell\), the sum over the set partitions of \(R\) of the products of \(\ell^{(B)}\) over the blocks. Then $$\partial_S E[\ell_a\ell_b] = E\Big[\sum_{T \subseteq S} \partial_T(\ell_a\ell_b)\, Y_{S \setminus T}\Big],\qquad \partial_T(\ell_a\ell_b) = \sum_{T = T_1 \sqcup T_2} \ell_{aT_1}\,\ell_{bT_2},$$ where the sums run over the subsets of the positions of \(S\). The terms are collected by their sorted factors. The highest derivative of \(\ell\) that appears is of order \(|S| + 1\).
